# Models account entry

This enhancement depends on the DSH 0.1.2 compatibility migration. It adds an optional `settings.models.footer` contribution, not a configurable-provider directory entry or a provider-card replacement. OAuth readiness is read from Codex Connect's account endpoint, never inferred from DSH's API-key credential indicator.

One `OpenAICodexAccountStore` is owned and disposed by the browser plugin. Models uses a compact provider-style row with state-dependent authorization controls and quota-only disclosure; Plugin settings retains its expanded controls. Subscribers share one status request and polling timer; the final unsubscribe aborts status observation. A pending login survives page navigation. Reopening joins the server's existing authorization, including from another trusted browser. A logout or cancellation invalidates older status reads. Plugin disposal stops polling and closes a pending blank popup without signing the server account out. The store never writes browser storage or handles bearer/refresh tokens.

The Models card keeps advanced configuration behind a More settings dialog. The dialog and original Plugin entry reuse `OpenAICodexConfiguration` and the same injected settings scope, including Save/Discard staging. Closing discards unsaved dialog edits. A native modal dialog contains keyboard focus; Escape closes only this dialog and returns focus to its trigger. Update controls remain in Plugin settings. The existing popup-blocked fallback, remote-origin warning, reauthorization and quota rendering are retained. No default model, search route, credential file or network trust policy is changed.

Authorization has a whole-flow deadline (10 minutes by default, configured by `oauthTimeoutMs` on load) as well as the initial URL deadline. The authenticated, origin-checked POST cancellation route does not delete credentials. Cancellation and new login are serialized until the old provider operation settles. The manual-code prompt observes both the provider prompt signal and the parent operation signal: pi-ai cancels its callback wait before awaiting manual input, so observing only its prompt signal would deadlock before provider cleanup. The installed provider's real cancellation state machine is exercised offline with only HTTP listen/close replaced; no real callback port, account or remote endpoint is used.

Validation includes existing account UI tests, shared-view synchronization and lifecycle tests, registration checks, and Chromium regressions for page switching, bidirectional settings persistence, draft disposal, keyboard focus, nested Escape and narrow-viewport layout. On 2026-08-31, the maintainer also completed and accepted real user OAuth and model/image validation. The registry installation and lockfile gates passed before Alpha 4.22 was marked ready for release.
